subject: english-language
topicDisplay: Unit 4: Personal or Creative Writing and Reading Literary and Non-fiction Texts
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Section A: Personal or Creative Writing
Section B: Reading Literary and Non-Fiction Texts
Writing accurately: spelling, punctuation and grammar
Analysing language and structure in texts

questions.q: In Section A, personal writing chiefly asks the candidate to do what?
options: Summarise an unseen non-fiction article
Draw on their own experiences, feelings and reflections
Analyse a poet's use of imagery
Compare the viewpoints of two writers
questions.explain: Personal writing is rooted in the candidate's own life, emotions and reflective thinking.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of creative writing suitable for Section A?
options: A short story or a piece of descriptive writing
A comparison of two newspaper reports
A summary of a travel guide
A comprehension answer on a poem
questions.explain: Creative writing includes imaginative forms such as short stories and descriptive pieces.

questions.q: What is the correct use of a semicolon?
options: To introduce a list after a clause
To join two closely related independent clauses
To show possession of a noun
To mark direct speech
questions.explain: A semicolon links two related independent clauses that could each stand alone as sentences.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-fiction text type candidates may meet in Section B?
options: A sonnet
An autobiography or an article
A fictional short story
A play script scene
questions.explain: Non-fiction includes factual and personal forms such as autobiographies, articles and travel writing.

questions.q: Which of the following would count as a literary text in Section B?
options: A supermarket advertisement
An extract from a novel
A set of instructions
A charity leaflet
questions.explain: Literary texts include prose fiction such as novel extracts, alongside poetry and drama.

questions.q: A simile creates a comparison by using which words?
options: 'is' or 'was'
'like' or 'as'
'and' or 'but'
'so' or 'because'
questions.explain: A simile compares two things explicitly using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
options: The dog's lead was too long
The dogs' lead was too long for one dog
Its' collar was red
The two dog's ran off
questions.explain: For a single owner the apostrophe goes before the 's' to show possession.

questions.q: Why should a candidate consider audience before beginning a creative piece?
options: To decide how many marks are available
To shape the tone, vocabulary and register appropriately
To count the number of paragraphs needed
To choose which examiner will read it
questions.explain: Awareness of audience guides tone, word choice and register so the writing suits its readers.

questions.q: What is the main effect of a metaphor compared with a simile?
options: It states one thing is another, creating a stronger, more direct image
It always makes a text funnier
It removes all description
It is only used in non-fiction
questions.explain: A metaphor equates one thing with another directly, producing a vivid and forceful image.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an engaging opening in a creative piece?
options: To list the events that will follow
To capture the reader's interest and draw them in
To state the word count
To name every character at once
questions.explain: A strong opening hooks the reader and encourages them to continue.

questions.q: When comparing two texts, a candidate should mainly focus on what?
options: Which text is longer
Similarities and differences in viewpoint, purpose and technique
The number of paragraphs in each
Which writer is more famous
questions.explain: Comparison requires exploring how the texts are alike and different in ideas and methods.

questions.q: Why is paragraphing important in a piece of personal writing?
options: It fills the page more quickly
It organises ideas and guides the reader through the writing
It removes the need for punctuation
It shows the reader where to stop reading
questions.explain: Paragraphs group related ideas and give the writing clear structure and flow.

questions.q: What does the 'tone' of a text refer to?
options: The number of adjectives used
The writer's attitude or feeling conveyed through language
The length of the sentences
The font the text is printed in
questions.explain: Tone is the attitude or mood a writer creates through their choice of language.

questions.q: Why might a writer vary their sentence lengths in a creative piece?
options: To reach the word count faster
To control pace and create effects such as tension or reflection
To avoid using paragraphs
To make spelling easier
questions.explain: Varying sentence length manipulates pace and can build tension or encourage reflection.

questions.q: In non-fiction, what is the purpose of a rhetorical question?
options: To gain factual information from the reader
To engage the reader and prompt them to think about the point
To end the text abruptly
To replace all punctuation
questions.explain: A rhetorical question involves the reader and encourages them to consider the writer's point.

questions.q: A student wants to build tension in a story. Which passage does this most effectively?
options: The door creaked. Silence. Then footsteps.
The door, which was rather old and had been painted several times over the years, made a noise as it opened slowly and steadily.
It was a nice day and everything felt calm and pleasant for everyone.
The house had four bedrooms, two bathrooms and a large garden at the back.
questions.explain: Short, sharp sentences quicken the pace and heighten tension.

questions.q: Which sentence uses sensory detail most effectively in a description?
options: The beach was nice and I liked it a lot.
The salty air stung my cheeks as gulls shrieked overhead.
There was a beach with sand and some water near it.
I went to the beach and then I went home again.
questions.explain: It appeals to touch, taste and sound, creating a vivid sensory image.

questions.q: Which device is used in the line 'The wind whispered through the trees'?
options: Simile
Personification
Hyperbole
Onomatopoeia
questions.explain: Giving the wind the human ability to whisper is personification.

questions.q: Which opening best suits a reflective personal essay about a childhood memory?
options: Firstly, I will explain the three key points of my essay.
Buy now while stocks last and save twenty per cent.
I still remember the smell of my grandmother's kitchen on those long summer afternoons.
The population of the town was around ten thousand people.
questions.explain: The reflective, first-person, sensory opening matches the purpose of a personal essay.

questions.q: A candidate must explain how a writer creates sympathy for a character. What should they mainly do?
options: Retell the whole plot in order
Select relevant quotations and explain the effect of the writer's language choices
Count the adjectives in the passage
Give their own opinion of the character without evidence
questions.explain: Analysis requires supporting points with quotations and explaining the effect of the language.
